workflow.contradiction.combworkMergesNee.text: Merging needs Git: without version control, work is accepted where it is.
workflow.contradiction.combworkMergesNee.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a merge option was set for a project with no version control.

workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol.text: “Committed is done” needs everyone in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.committedNeedsFol.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Committed is done” was chosen while each card has its own folder.

workflow.contradiction.focusedNeedsRunne.text: Each card’s focused tests need the command that runs them.
workflow.contradiction.focusedNeedsRunne.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved (G20): “Each card’s focused tests” is on but the project has no command to run them (its runner, focused.run).

workflow.contradiction.jjNeedsSlots.text: With jj, each card needs its own folder: agents sharing the project folder aren’t supported yet.
workflow.contradiction.jjNeedsSlots.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved (HI-2799): a project using jj (Jujutsu) was set to have everyone work in the project folder. Keep jj (the tool’s name).

workflow.contradiction.jjYouIntegrate.text: With jj, you integrate the reviewed work yourself: Combwork doesn’t merge it.
workflow.contradiction.jjYouIntegrate.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved (HI-2799): a project using jj (Jujutsu) had another finish chosen than “You integrate it”. Keep jj (the tool’s name).

workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots.text: When Combwork or the agent merges, each card needs its own folder.
workflow.contradiction.mergeNeedsSlots.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a merging option was chosen while everyone works in the project folder.

workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots.text: Without version control, everyone works in the project folder.
workflow.contradiction.noneHasNoSlots.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: separate folders per card were set for a project with no version control.

workflow.contradiction.okWithReview.text: Your OK before merging is already part of review by you.
workflow.contradiction.okWithReview.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: the user's OK before merging was set while the user already reviews.

workflow.contradiction.poolNeedsAgent.text: A shared pool of reviewers needs review by reviewer agents.
workflow.contradiction.poolNeedsAgent.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Reviewers” was set to a shared pool (reviewer agents lanes share) without review by reviewer agents.

workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent.text: Two reviewers per card need review by reviewer agents.
workflow.contradiction.quorumNeedsAgent.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: two reviewers per card were set without reviewer agents.

workflow.contradiction.selfReview.text: “Nobody reviews their own work” can't be off while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.contradiction.selfReview.note: Why workflow options in the Version Control tab cannot be saved: the no-self-review option was turned off while a reviewer agent is required.

workflow.contradiction.subfolderTarget.text: This project is inside a larger repository: name the branch its work merges into.
workflow.contradiction.subfolderTarget.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved (OP-29): Combwork or the agent merges, but the project is a subfolder of a bigger Git repository and its own options name no target branch (merges would affect the whole repository).

workflow.contradiction.upToDateNeedsSlot.text: Slots are brought up to date only when each card has its own folder.
workflow.contradiction.upToDateNeedsSlot.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: “Slots are brought up to date before each card” (G15) was set while everyone works in the project folder (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.focused.programMissing.text: Combwork couldn't find the program this command starts: {command}
workflow.focused.programMissing.note: The focused-test picker's diagnostics: its command's program isn't found. command: the command as written.

workflow.focused.resultsUnread.note: A check's output: the focused tests' runner wrote results that couldn't be read. why: what was wrong with them.

workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge.text: {card} was decided after it merged: does it need a follow-up?
workflow.forYou.decidedAfterMerge.note: A For you request (Decide): a decision was recorded on the card while its work was being merged, so the merged work didn't see it. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.focusedSkip.text: {card}’s focused tests were skipped at its merge: {tests}. Merge it with them skipped?
workflow.forYou.focusedSkip.note: A For you request (Approve, G20, HI-1367): the merge queue ran the card’s focused tests ({tests}: test names, each with why it was skipped in brackets, as its project’s runner said) and some were skipped for their environment (a usage limit, a sign-in, the network). Approve merges the card with them skipped; Decline returns it. The card’s reviewer agent is asked too.

workflow.forYou.lineAsk.text: {line} still has {card}'s work, squashed into {target}: approve and Combwork brings the branch up to date once, or decline and do it yourself before {next} starts.
workflow.forYou.lineAsk.note: A For you request (approve or decline, §16.19.2): Settings → Advanced has Combwork ask before moving an agent's branch after a squash merge. Approving lets Combwork move it this once (git reset --keep, which never overwrites uncommitted work); declining leaves it to the user. {line} a branch name; {card} and {next} card keys like AM-12; {target} the branch merged into.

workflow.forYou.lineRefused.text: Git wouldn't bring {line} up to date with {target}: {reason}. {next} starts once the branch is up to date.
workflow.forYou.lineRefused.note: A For you request (Decide, §16.19.2): Combwork tried to move the builder's branch after a squash merge and git refused; the lane waits. {line} a branch name, {target} the branch merged into, {reason} git's own message (English), {next} a card key.

workflow.forYou.lineUnfinished.text: Combwork's move of {line} to {to} didn't finish and couldn't be put back. Bring the branch to {target} with its files and index clean, or back where it was: {next} starts once it is settled.
workflow.forYou.lineUnfinished.note: A For you request (Decide, §16.19.2): moving the builder's branch failed part way and Combwork couldn't undo it, so the branch, its files or its index may disagree; the lane waits. {line} a branch name, {to} a short commit id, {target} the branch merged into, {next} a card key.

workflow.forYou.lineWork.text: {line} has work that isn't in {target}: {commits}. Decide what happens to it: {next} starts once the branch is up to date.
workflow.forYou.lineWork.note: A For you request (Decide, §16.19.2): the builder's branch has commits that weren't merged (made after the card was approved, say), so Combwork won't move the branch and lose them; the lane waits. {line} a branch name, {target} the branch merged into, {commits} a list of short commit ids with their subjects, {next} a card key.

workflow.forYou.mergeChoice.text: How should Combwork merge {project}'s cards into {target}? Choose the merge style and the commit message: until now Combwork made a merge commit with its own message (the card's key and title, with trailers). The merge queue waits for your answer.
workflow.forYou.mergeChoice.note: A For you request (Decide, HI-1697): a project from before 1.0 reached the merge queue for the first time, and nobody chose how its cards are merged, so the queue asks. {project} is a project's name, {target} the branch merged into. Merge style and Commit message are workflow options' names (glossary 2.6): use their words. Trailers: git's “Key: value” lines at a message's end.

workflow.forYou.newDecision.text: {card} has a new decision: your review again?
workflow.forYou.newDecision.note: A For you request: the user decided something new on a card in Review, so their review is asked again. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.okBefore.note: A For you request: the card passed review and waits for the user's OK before it merges (glossary 2.3: approval). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.passedReview.note: A For you request: reviewer agents passed the card, and the user reviews after them (A reviewer agent, then you). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.queueAdvance.text: {card} is tested and ready to merge: update {target} in {folder} now?
workflow.forYou.queueAdvance.note: A For you request (Approve, §16.9.2): the merge queue has merged and checked the card's work, and waits for the user's OK before it updates the branch {target}, which is checked out in the folder {folder} (its files change there). Settings → Advanced → Merge into a checked-out branch: Ask each time. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.queueCatchUp.text: {card} is merged and on {target}’s remote already: update {target} in {folder} to it now? Decline, and {target} there stays as it is until you pull.
workflow.forYou.queueCatchUp.note: A For you request (Approve, HI-3092, “The target branch follows its remote”): a card ({card}: a key like AM-12) was found already merged on the remote branch the target ({target}: a branch) follows, so it is Done; the local {target}, checked out in the folder {folder} (its files change there), is behind it. Settings → Advanced → Merge into a checked-out branch: Ask each time, so the queue waits for the user's OK before it updates that folder. Declined: nothing changes there; the user pulls when they want.

workflow.forYou.queuePublish.text: Combwork pushed {card} ({result}) to {endpoint} for {target}, but never heard whether the push arrived, and {target} there doesn’t show it now. Approve if {result} was published (someone may have removed it since); decline if it wasn’t, and the queue tests {card} again. Until you answer, the queue for {target} waits.
workflow.forYou.queuePublish.note: A For you request (Approve, HI-1183, §16.9.4, “The target branch follows its remote”): the merge queue pushed a merge to the remote, the push’s answer was lost (the network, a crash), and the remote’s branch doesn’t contain it now, so Combwork can’t tell whether it was published and asks. {card} a card key like AM-12; {result} a short commit id; {endpoint} the remote’s address without credentials; {target} the branch.

workflow.forYou.queueStuck.text: {card}'s merge into {target} stopped part way in {folder}, with {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} left between the two, and Combwork changes nothing more there. The card's Work section lists each file and its side, and the commands to copy. {how, select, both {To finish it, run {finish} (PowerShell) in {project}; to undo it, run {undo} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} finish {To finish it, run {finish} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} undo {To undo it, run {undo} (PowerShell) in {folder}.} other {Its files are neither as they were nor as merged: put them right by hand.}} Then answer here, and the queue looks again.
workflow.forYou.queueStuck.note: A For you request (Decide, §16.9.2's terminal state): the merge queue was updating the branch {target}, checked out in the folder {folder}, and something (a crash, another program) left it half done, so the merge queue for {target} is paused until the user settles it. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {files} how many files the merge left part way; the card's Work section is a section of the card's dialog (glossary 2.4: work); {project} the project folder; {finish} and {undo} are git commands for PowerShell (keep them exactly, with (PowerShell) after them). Translate each choice of {how}; keep the codes before the braces.

workflow.forYou.review.note: A For you request: the card waits for the user to review it (Version Control → Work is reviewed before it is merged: You). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.forYou.roundLimit.text: {card} failed {rounds, plural, one {# review} other {# reviews}}: carry on with more rounds, split it, accept it with follow-ups, or take it over?
workflow.forYou.roundLimit.note: A For you request (Decide): the card reached its card loop's round limit (Settings → Card loops), so its loop pauses until the user chooses one of four ways on. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {rounds} the reviews it failed (a number).

workflow.forYou.slotDirty.text: {card} is Done, but {slot} has uncommitted changes, so it stays on {line}. Commit or discard them there: Combwork then detaches the slot at {target}, ready for its next card.
workflow.forYou.slotDirty.note: A For you request (Decide, HI-2014): a card reached Done while its slot (a reused working folder, such as slot-b) had uncommitted changes, so Combwork left the slot on the card's branch {line} instead of detaching it at the target branch {target}. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {slot}, {line} and {target} are names, kept as they are.

workflow.forYouKind.text: {kind, select, approve {Approve} decide {Decide} test {Test} signIn {Sign in} other {Other}}
workflow.forYouKind.note: The kind of a request for the user (For you), shown as its label: approve something, decide something, test something, sign in somewhere, or anything else. Translate each choice; keep the codes before the braces.

workflow.jj.containment.text: whether a jj card's change is in its target (decided by jj's integration proof, not enabled yet)
workflow.jj.containment.note: HI-2868: what Combwork couldn't read for a jj project's card: containment in its target is decided by a later card's proof.

workflow.jj.notYet.text: a jj project's card work (not enabled yet)
workflow.jj.notYet.note: HI-2799: what Combwork couldn't read for a card of a project using jj: its card work isn't enabled yet.

workflow.jj.start.carryTarget.text: its earlier work is in slot {slot} on {target}
workflow.jj.start.carryTarget.note: HI-2868: why a restarted jj card could not start: its earlier work is still in its slot, on another target bookmark. {slot} is the slot name, {target} the bookmark.

workflow.jj.start.inGit.text: the slot is inside the Git repository at {root}, which git commands in it would reach
workflow.jj.start.inGit.note: HI-2896: why a jj card could not start: its slot of a jj repository not colocated with Git is inside a Git working tree ({root}, made or moved there after the switch).

workflow.jj.start.noSlot.note: HI-2868: why a jj card could not start: its builder was lent no slot.

workflow.jj.start.notWorkspace.text: the slot is not a jj workspace Combwork made
workflow.jj.start.notWorkspace.note: HI-2868: why a jj card could not start: its slot folder is not a workspace Combwork made.

workflow.jj.start.slots.note: HI-2868: why a jj card could not start: the project does not give cards slots.

workflow.jj.start.target.text: a jj project needs a target bookmark (Work merges into)
workflow.jj.start.target.note: HI-2868: why a jj card could not start: no target bookmark is set. Work merges into is a name in the window.

workflow.move.answer.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user's answer to a For you request (Approve, Decline, a reply).

workflow.move.declarePaths.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: saying which files are its work (a project without version control).

workflow.move.loopStep.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move (#1382): a step between a card loop's builder and reviewer that moves nothing (a design posted for a check, its answer).

workflow.move.move.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: dragging it to another column.

workflow.move.putBack.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: putting a started card back in Todo.

workflow.move.removeFromQueue.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user taking it out of the merge queue.

workflow.move.reportMerge.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the agent saying it merged the work.

workflow.move.resolveOnBuilder.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move (HI-2959): the user's Resolve on a builder on a forward merge the merge queue returned (Combwork's card bringing one branch up to date with another): it ends, and a new card is made for a builder to resolve its conflict.

workflow.move.retryMerge.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: the user's Retry merge on the merge queue's card.

workflow.move.start.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move ("… isn't possible from there"): starting work on it.

workflow.move.startReview.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: a reviewer beginning a review.

workflow.move.submit.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: sending its work to Review.

workflow.move.verdict.note: A move on a card, named in a refused move: a reviewer passing or failing it (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.option.commands.desc.text: The command each named check runs. A run counts as the check only when it runs that command.
workflow.option.commands.desc.note: What the workflow setting “Check commands” does.

workflow.option.commands.title.note: A workflow setting: the command each named check runs (the checks of “Checks pass before review”).

workflow.option.commitMessage.desc.text: The message of the commit the merge queue makes: Combwork’s names the card’s key and title and adds Combwork’s trailers, and the branch’s own uses the message its commits have, with no card key or trailers, while Combwork still knows which card it merged.
workflow.option.commitMessage.desc.note: What the workflow option “Commit message” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue). Trailers are git’s name for the “Key: value” lines at the end of a commit message: keep the word if your language’s git terms do.

workflow.option.commitMessage.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G19): the message of the commit Combwork’s merge queue makes when it merges a card (a merge commit, or a squash’s one commit).

workflow.option.dependenciesDone.desc.text: A card that waits for others can’t start before their work is in.
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.desc.note: What the workflow option “Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged” does.

workflow.option.dependenciesDone.none.text: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.none.note: A workflow option for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N6).

workflow.option.dependenciesDone.title.text: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged

workflow.option.excluded.desc.text: The whole project folder, apart from these folders and files (.combwork always).
workflow.option.excluded.desc.note: What the workflow option “What the work is” does: the folders and files listed are left out of a card’s work.

workflow.option.excluded.title.note: A workflow option for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N4).

workflow.option.fileLocks.desc.text: What happens when an agent tries to edit a file another agent in the same folder is editing.
workflow.option.fileLocks.desc.note: What the workflow option “File locks” does.

workflow.option.fileLocks.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, N7): what happens when two agents in the same folder edit the same file.

workflow.option.finish.desc.text: When a card is done: once Combwork’s merge queue has merged it, once its agent has merged it and Combwork finds the work in the target branch, once it is committed, or whenever it is moved there.
workflow.option.finish.desc.note: What the workflow option “Who merges” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.option.focusedTests.desc.text: When a card is submitted, the project’s command chooses the tests its change needs (or its builder names them, for its reviewer to check), and the merge queue runs them on the merged result, moving the target only once they pass.
workflow.option.focusedTests.desc.note: What the workflow option “Each card’s focused tests pass on the merged result” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.option.focusedTests.title.text: Each card’s focused tests pass on the merged result
workflow.option.focusedTests.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G20): the tests a card’s change needs are chosen when it is submitted, and Combwork’s merge queue runs them on its work merged with the target branch.

workflow.option.folder.desc.text: In its own folder, a slot Combwork lends to the card or its lane, each card is built on a branch of its own, apart from other agents’ work; in the project folder, everyone sees each other’s unfinished changes.
workflow.option.folder.desc.note: What the workflow option “Where cards are built” does (glossary 2.5: slot, a worktree Combwork lends to a card or a lane).

workflow.option.followRemote.desc.text: Before each test merge, the merge queue fetches the remote branch the target tracks and tests on its latest commit, pushes each merge there only if nobody pushed meanwhile (testing again if they did), and then brings the local target up to date.
workflow.option.followRemote.desc.note: What the workflow option “The target branch follows its remote” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue; 2.5: test merge). “Push the target branch after merging” is another option’s name.

workflow.option.followRemote.title.text: The target branch follows its remote
workflow.option.followRemote.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G21): the target branch is the one it tracks on its remote; Combwork’s merge queue fetches it before each test merge and publishes each merge there first.

workflow.option.identity.desc.text: Commits are made with the name and email from the project’s git config (else your global one).
workflow.option.identity.desc.note: What the workflow option “Commits use the project’s identity” does.

workflow.option.loopRounds.desc.text: How many rounds a card gets in a card loop (a build and its review each) before its agents stop and ask you, when the loop doesn’t say.
workflow.option.loopRounds.desc.note: What the workflow option “Rounds” does (Card loops).

workflow.option.loopRounds.title.note: A workflow option, under Card loops: how many rounds (a build and its review) a card gets before its agents ask you.

workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.desc.text: How many minutes, up to 4 hours, a card loop’s builder waits for its reviewer to check a design it posted before it goes ahead as posted.
workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.desc.note: What the workflow option “Design check wait (minutes)” does (Card loops). A design: the plan a builder posts on its card before building.

workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.titl.note: A workflow option, under Card loops: how long a builder waits for its reviewer to check a design it posted.

workflow.option.loopWaitHours.desc.text: How many hours, up to a day, an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you, when the loop doesn’t say.
workflow.option.loopWaitHours.desc.note: What the workflow option “Wait (hours)” does (Card loops).

workflow.option.loopWaitHours.title.note: A workflow option, under Card loops: how many hours an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you.

workflow.option.loopWakes.desc.text: When a card with a reviewer arrives in Review, Combwork wakes the reviewer, and on the review’s verdict the card’s builder; off, only the agents’ own card watches wake them.
workflow.option.loopWakes.desc.note: What the workflow option “Wake reviewers and builders” does.

workflow.option.loopWakes.title.note: A workflow option, under Card loops: Combwork wakes the agents of a card loop for its handoffs (glossary: card loop).

workflow.option.maxAgents.desc.text: Your team size: the most agents this project has, whoever adds them (you, the Assistant or a program using the Agent API), and lowering it removes none.
workflow.option.maxAgents.desc.note: What the workflow option “Maximum agents” does (HI-2058: it binds the user too). Agent API is the name of a Combwork feature.

workflow.option.maxAgents.title.note: A workflow option (HI-2001): the most agents the project has, its team size. Nobody adds agents past it: the user, the Combwork Assistant or a program (HI-2058).

workflow.option.mergeChecks.desc.text: Combwork’s merge queue runs these named commands on the card’s work merged with the target branch, and moves the target only once each one has passed.
workflow.option.mergeChecks.desc.note: What the workflow option “Checks pass on the merged result” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue).

workflow.option.mergeChecks.jjDesc.text: Combwork runs these named commands on the candidate, in a check copy of its own, and offers the candidate for you to integrate only once each one has passed. One that fails sends the card back to its builder.
workflow.option.mergeChecks.jjDesc.note: What the workflow option “Checks pass on the candidate” does, for a project using jj (HI-2938). A check copy is a working folder Combwork keeps for checks (glossary).

workflow.option.mergeChecks.jjTitle.note: The workflow option “Checks pass on the merged result” (G9) for a project using jj (HI-2938): named commands Combwork runs on the candidate it builds for the user to integrate. Candidate: the commit Combwork builds.

workflow.option.mergeChecks.title.text: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.option.mergeChecks.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G9): named commands Combwork’s merge queue runs on a card’s work merged with the target branch.

workflow.option.mergeInstall.desc.text: Before the checks on the merged result, the merge queue installs the dependencies afresh, and always does when the lock file or manifests changed.
workflow.option.mergeInstall.desc.note: What the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” does. Lock file: as in the glossary (G15 value).

workflow.option.mergeInstall.jjDesc.text: Before the checks on a candidate, its check copy installs the dependencies afresh: always, or when the lock file or manifests changed.
workflow.option.mergeInstall.jjDesc.note: What the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” does, for a project using jj (HI-2938). A check copy is a working folder Combwork keeps for checks. Lock file: as in the glossary.

workflow.option.mergeInstall.jjTitle.note: The workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” for a project using jj (HI-2938): before the checks on the candidate.

workflow.option.mergeInstall.title.note: A workflow option (G9’s install): when the merge queue installs the project’s dependencies afresh before the merge checks.

workflow.option.noSelfReview.desc.text: Always on while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.option.noSelfReview.desc.note: What the workflow option “Nobody reviews their own work” does.

workflow.option.noSelfReview.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G2 and N2).

workflow.option.okBefore.desc.text: A card waits for your OK before it is merged: never, only cards with these labels, or every card.
workflow.option.okBefore.desc.note: What the workflow option “Your OK before merging” does.

workflow.option.otherTargets.desc.text: Branches a lane or a card can merge into instead (its Merges into), each through its own merge queue with the same merge checks, separated by commas.
workflow.option.otherTargets.desc.note: What the workflow option “Other branches work can merge into” does (HI-2556). Merges into is the lane’s and card’s field: as translated there.

workflow.option.otherTargets.title.text: Other branches work can merge into
workflow.option.otherTargets.title.note: A workflow option (HI-2556, G7b): branches besides “Work merges into” that a lane or a card can be set to merge into (its “Merges into”). Darren’s name for it.

workflow.option.preChecks.desc.text: A card goes to review only once each of these named commands has passed on its work.
workflow.option.preChecks.desc.note: What the workflow option “Checks pass before review” does.

workflow.option.preChecks.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G3 and N3): named commands that must pass before a card goes to review.

workflow.option.pushTarget.desc.text: After each merge, the merge queue pushes the target branch to the remote it tracks (or the only remote, or origin), never forced, and pauses, saying why, when the push is refused or fails.
workflow.option.pushTarget.desc.note: What the workflow option “Push the target branch after merging” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue). Origin is git’s usual name for a remote: keep it.

workflow.option.pushTarget.title.text: Push the target branch after merging
workflow.option.pushTarget.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G18): after Combwork’s merge queue merges a card, it pushes the target branch to its remote.

workflow.option.review.desc.text: A card goes to Review when its builder submits it and moves on only once it passes, waiting for your OK after the reviewer when you check too.
workflow.option.review.desc.note: What the workflow option “Work is reviewed before it’s merged” does.

workflow.option.review.none.text: Who checks the work before it’s done
workflow.option.review.none.note: A workflow option for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N1).

workflow.option.review.shared.text: Work is reviewed before it’s done
workflow.option.review.shared.note: The workflow option G1 when everyone works in the project folder, where the work is on the target meanwhile (glossary 2.6, G1 shared folder).

workflow.option.review.title.text: Work is reviewed before it’s merged
workflow.option.review.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G1): who reviews a card’s work before it is merged.

workflow.option.reviewerMode.desc.text: One reviewer per lane, or a shared pool: Combwork gives each card submitted in a pool lane, oldest first, to the next free reviewer that didn’t build it.
workflow.option.reviewerMode.desc.note: What the workflow option “Reviewers” does (glossary 2.6, G17; glossary: lane, pool).

workflow.option.reviewerMode.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G17): whether each lane has its own reviewer agent or the lanes share a pool of reviewers.

workflow.option.reviewers.desc.text: With two, both must pass the same change.
workflow.option.reviewers.desc.note: What the workflow option “Reviewers per card” does.

workflow.option.reviewers.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G1b): how many reviewer agents must pass a card.

workflow.option.sameness.desc.text: With Same change, a pass carries over to a clean rebase or squash of the same change; with Exact revision only, any new revision makes it stale.
workflow.option.sameness.desc.note: What the workflow option “A pass survives a clean rebase” does.

workflow.option.sameness.title.text: A pass survives a clean rebase

workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.desc.text: A submit warns, never refuses, when its commit takes in files another agent is editing in the project folder.
workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.desc.note: What the workflow option “Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files” does.

workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.titl.text: Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files

workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.desc.text: Before a card starts in a slot, the slot is brought to the latest work of the target branch, and its dependencies are installed again when the lock file changed.
workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.desc.note: What the workflow option “Slots are brought up to date before each card” does (glossary 2.5: slot; lock file, as in the G15 value).

workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.title.text: Slots are brought up to date before each card
workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G15; glossary 2.5: slot): before a card starts in a slot, the slot is brought to the target branch’s latest work.

workflow.option.stageNames.desc.text: Rename any stage the board shows: a name changes no rule and applies at once.
workflow.option.stageNames.desc.note: What the workflow option “Stage names” does (glossary 2.2: stage).

workflow.option.stageNames.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, N5; glossary 2.2: stage): your own names for the board’s stages.

workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.desc.text: A card goes to review only once its builder’s own runs and background commands have stopped.
workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.desc.note: What the workflow option “Agents stop what they started before review” does.

workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.title.text: Agents stop what they started before review

workflow.option.strict.desc.text: When the target branch has moved on since the review, the merge queue brings the work up to date in its own folder first, and returns the card if that conflicts or makes a different change.
workflow.option.strict.desc.note: What the workflow option “Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges” does (glossary 2.1: merge queue; Squash is the merge style’s value).

workflow.option.strict.jjDesc.text: When the target bookmark has moved on since the review, Combwork first brings the work up to date with it (merged in, or rebased with Squash), then builds the candidate on that, and returns the card if that conflicts or makes a different change. Rebase builds its candidate on the bookmark anyway.
workflow.option.strict.jjDesc.note: What the workflow option “The candidate brings work up to date first” does, for a project using jj (HI-2871). A bookmark is jj’s name for a branch; Squash and Rebase are the candidate style’s values.

workflow.option.strict.jjTitle.text: The candidate brings work up to date first
workflow.option.strict.jjTitle.note: The workflow option “Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges” (G8, strict) for a project using jj (HI-2871): before building the candidate the user integrates, Combwork brings the card’s work up to date with the target bookmark.

workflow.option.strict.title.text: Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges
workflow.option.strict.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G8, strict): a card’s work must contain the target branch’s latest commit before it is merged; Combwork’s merge queue brings it up to date itself.

workflow.option.style.desc.text: How a card’s work is merged into the target branch.
workflow.option.style.desc.note: What the workflow option “Merge style” does.

workflow.option.style.jjDesc.text: Once a card passes, Combwork builds a candidate from it on the target bookmark: a merge commit, one squashed commit, or its commits copied on top. You move the bookmark to the candidate yourself; Combwork never does.
workflow.option.style.jjDesc.note: What the workflow option “Candidate style” does, for a project using jj (HI-2871). A bookmark is jj’s name for a branch: keep it as jj’s term.

workflow.option.style.jjTitle.note: The workflow option “Merge style” (G6) for a project using jj (HI-2871): how the candidate commit Combwork builds for the user to integrate is made (merge commit, squash or rebase). Candidate: the commit Combwork builds.

workflow.option.target.desc.text: The branch a card’s work is merged into: the repository’s default branch when left empty.
workflow.option.target.desc.note: What the workflow option “Work merges into” does.

workflow.option.target.title.note: A workflow option (glossary 2.6, G7): the target branch.

workflow.refused.approval.given.change.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Your OK before merging.
workflow.refused.approval.given.change.note: Where the rule that waits for the user's OK is changed.

workflow.refused.approval.given.message.text: {card} waits for the OK before merging.
workflow.refused.approval.given.message.note: A refused move: the user has to approve the card first (glossary 2.3: approval; Version Control → Your OK before merging).

workflow.refused.approval.given.next.text: Wait for the OK, given on the card or in For you.
workflow.refused.approval.given.next.note: The next step after a move refused for want of the user’s approval.

workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.messag.text: A plain number is not a card reference.
workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.messag.note: A refused intent: the card was named by a bare number.

workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.next.text: Name the card by its key: {key}.
workflow.refused.card.plainNumber.next.note: How to name a card instead of a bare number: by its key, {key} (such as AM-12).

workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..text: {why, select, ambiguous {{revision} is the start of more than one commit here: give more of it. {head} is checked out.} other {{revision} isn't what's checked out here: {head} is.}}
workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..note: A refused check run or submission (HI-2671): the revision named ({revision}, as given, a commit id or its start) is not the checked-out commit ({head}, its first 12 characters). why=ambiguous: {revision} is the start of the checked-out commit but also of another one, so more of its characters are needed.

workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..text: Run the check where {revision} is checked out, or without a revision.
workflow.refused.check.revisionMismatch..note: The next step after a check run named the wrong revision.

workflow.refused.done.contained.change.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges.
workflow.refused.done.contained.change.note: Where the rule that checks a merge is changed.

workflow.refused.done.contained.message.note: A refused Done: the approved revision is not in the target branch. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.done.contained.next.text: Merge {revision} into {target}, then report the merge again.
workflow.refused.done.contained.next.note: The next step after a refused report of a merge.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag.text: What Combwork read for {card} changed while it decided.
workflow.refused.evidence.changed.messag.note: A refused intent: a branch head, a file or another card the rule depends on changed between Combwork's reading it and recording the move. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.evidence.changed.next.text: Try again: Combwork reads it afresh.
workflow.refused.evidence.changed.next.note: The next step after a refusal because what a rule read changed meanwhile.

workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.messa.text: {card} brings one branch up to date with another: only the user or the Assistant acts on it.
workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.messa.note: HI-2679: a refused intent: an agent acted on a forward-merge card (Combwork’s own card that merges one of the project’s target branches into another). {card} is its key (HI-12).

workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.next.text: Leave it to the user or the Assistant.
workflow.refused.forward.notAgents.next.note: HI-2679: the next step after an agent was refused acting on a forward-merge card.

workflow.refused.forward.resolutionSourc.text: {card} resolves the merge of {from} into {to}, but {revision} doesn’t contain {source}, the commit that came back: a cherry-pick or a copy of its changes leaves it out of {to}’s history, so the next Bring Up to Date would conflict again.
workflow.refused.forward.resolutionSourc.note: HI-2999: a refused submission of a card made by Resolve on a builder (it merges branch {from} into branch {to} by hand): the revision submitted ({revision}, a short commit id) doesn’t have the commit it resolves ({source}, a full commit id) in its history. Bring Up to Date is a command’s name in the window: as translated there. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.forward.resolutionSourc.text: In its branch, run git merge {source}, resolve the conflict, commit, and submit again.
workflow.refused.forward.resolutionSourc.note: HI-2999: the next step after that refusal: merge the commit ({source}, a full commit id; "git merge" is a command, never translated) into the card’s branch.

workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.text: {card} resolves the merge of {from} into {to}, but it would start from {target} and merge there.
workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.note: HI-2985: a refused start of a card made by Resolve on a builder (it merges branch {from} into branch {to} by hand): its Merges into is another branch now ({target}), as when the project’s Work merges into moved on after it was made. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.text: The user or the Assistant can set its Merges into to {to}, then start it again.
workflow.refused.forward.resolutionTarge.note: HI-2985: the next step after a refused start of a Resolve on a builder card: set its Merges into (a name in the window: as translated there) to branch {to}.

workflow.refused.integrate.approved.mess.note: A refused merge: the revision lacks the passes or approvals its rules need. {why} is a whole sentence saying what's missing.

workflow.refused.integrate.approved.next.note: The next step after a merge refused for want of approval.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..text: This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass on the merged result.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..note: Where the merge checks are changed.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..text: The merge checks failed on {card}'s merged result.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..note: A merge returned: the merge checks failed on the test merge.

workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..text: Fix the failures, commit and submit the new revision.
workflow.refused.integrate.checksPassed..note: The next step after failed merge checks.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.chan.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Work is up to date before it merges.
workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.chan.note: Where the strict rule is changed.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.mess.note: A refused merge (strict): the revision is behind its target. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.next.text: The merge queue brings it up to date itself.
workflow.refused.integrate.upToDate.next.note: What happens next after the strict up-to-date rule refuses.

workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.change.text: Settings → Advanced → Bring an agent's branch up to date after a squash merge says whether Combwork moves it or asks first.
workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.change.note: Where it is decided whether Combwork moves the branch itself or asks the user first (a setting name: use it as Combwork shows it).

workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.message.text: {card} can't start yet: {line} still has {earlier}'s work, which was squashed into {target}.
workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.message.note: A refused start (§16.19.2): the builder's branch (in its own worktree) still has the previous card's commits, which were merged into the target as one squashed commit, so the next card's change would include them. {card} and {earlier} are card keys like AM-12; {line} a branch name; {target} the branch merged into.

workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.next.text: {reader, select, you {Leave it as it is: Combwork brings {line} up to date with {target} once the agent is idle, or asks you first, and tells the agent when {card} can start.} other {Leave it as it is: Combwork brings {line} up to date with {target} once you are idle, or asks the user, and tells you when {card} can start.}}
workflow.refused.lane.lineBehind.next.note: The next step after a start refused because the branch still has squashed work: wait (end the turn); Combwork moves the branch, or asks the user first, and says when the card can start. {line} a branch name, {target} the branch merged into, {card} a card key. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.change.text: A lane always takes one card at a time; turning off Settings → Advanced → Workflow rules are enforced turns every rule off.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.change.note: Where the rule that a lane takes one card at a time is changed: it has no option of its own; the switch that turns every workflow rule off (a setting name: use it as Combwork shows it).

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.message.text: {card} can't start yet: {earlier}, before it in its lane, isn't Done.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.message.note: A refused start (glossary 2.4): a lane takes one card at a time, so a card starts only once the cards before it in its lane are Done. {card} and {earlier} are card keys like AM-12.

workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.next.text: Finish {earlier} first: once it is Done, the lane goes on to {card}.
workflow.refused.lane.oneAtATime.next.note: The next step after a start refused because an earlier card of the lane is not Done. {card} and {earlier} are card keys like AM-12.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.me.text: {card}: a follow-up waits for its reviewer's check, with no going ahead without it.
workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.me.note: A refused going ahead unchecked (#1467): what waits is a follow-up (a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's), which only its reviewer's answer settles. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.ne.text: {reader, select, you {The agent waits for the reviewer's ok or gaps; if none comes, it asks you.} other {Wait for the reviewer's ok or gaps; if none comes, ask the user.}}
workflow.refused.loop.followUpChecked.ne.note: The next step after going ahead with a follow-up unchecked (#1467). ok and gaps are the reviewer's answers, as agents name them: keep them as they are. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.me.text: {card} is being merged now: a follow-up can no longer take it out of the merge queue.
workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.me.note: A refused follow-up (#1623): a follow-up on a queued card takes it out of the merge queue first, but the queue has already begun merging this one. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.ne.text: Wait for the merge; if the follow-up is still needed, put it on a new card.
workflow.refused.loop.followUpMerging.ne.note: The next step after a follow-up refused because the card is being merged now (#1623).

workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.message.text: {card} has no reviewer to check it: it is in no lane with a reviewer, and nobody has reviewed it yet.
workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.message.note: A refused design or follow-up posted for a check (#1382, #1467): nobody can be woken to check it. {card} is a card key. A lane: a card loop's record of its builder and reviewer.

workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.next.text: Start a lane for the card with a reviewer, or say it in a comment instead.
workflow.refused.loop.noReviewer.next.note: The next step after a design or follow-up refused for want of a reviewer (#1382, #1467).

workflow.refused.loop.noStep.message.text: {card} has no design or follow-up waiting for its check.
workflow.refused.loop.noStep.message.note: A refused card loop step (#1382, #1467): an answer (OK, gaps) or going ahead when no design or follow-up posted by its builder waits for its reviewer's check. A follow-up: a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.noStep.next.text: Read the card: it may have been answered, or the card moved on. Feedback still worth giving goes on the card as a comment.
workflow.refused.loop.noStep.next.note: The next step after a card loop step with nothing to answer (#1382): what was posted for the check may have been answered, or the card left the column it was posted in (HI-3011: a design closes when its card is put back). A reviewer with feedback for it comments on the card instead.

workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.message.text: {card} reached its round limit: it goes on once its round-limit question is answered.
workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.message.note: A refused submission or move: the card failed as many reviews as its card loop allows (Settings → Card loops), and Combwork asked how to go on (For you); until that question is answered, its loop is paused. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one (never "the user"). {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.next.text: The question is on the card (For you): once it is answered, Combwork wakes the agents waiting on it.
workflow.refused.loop.roundLimit.next.note: The next step while a card waits at its round limit for its question (For you, a label: use it as Combwork shows it) to be answered. Read by agents and shown in the window alike: it names no one (never "the user"); Combwork then wakes the agents that wait on the card.

workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.message.text: {card}: that is about {design}, but the one waiting for its check now is {waiting}.
workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.message.note: A refused answer to a design or follow-up, or going ahead with a design (#1382, #1467): it names an earlier one than the one waiting now, so it can't settle it. {card} is a card key; {design} and {waiting} are their ids, such as AM-12/s40.

workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.next.text: Read the card's latest comment and answer the one it names.
workflow.refused.loop.staleStep.next.note: The next step after an answer to an earlier design or follow-up (#1382, #1467).

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.messag.text: {step, select, followUp {{card} is in {stage}: a follow-up is posted for its check once the work is in review or has passed it.} other {{card} is in {stage}: a design is posted for its check before the work goes to review.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.messag.note: A refused card loop step (#1382, #1467): a design was posted for a card that isn't being worked on (not in Doing), or a follow-up (a change asked of reviewed work, such as a screenshot's) for a card that isn't in Review or Passed. {card} is a card key; {stage} the stage it is in; step (select): followUp, or other for a design. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.next.text: {step, select, followUp {Send the work to review, or say it in a comment.} other {Post it while the card is being worked on, or say it in a comment.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotHere.next.note: The next step after a design posted for a card that is not being worked on, or a follow-up for a card not in Review or Passed (#1382, #1467). step (select): followUp, or other for a design. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.messa.text: {side, select, builder {Only the builder of {card} posts its design or follow-up, or goes ahead with a design.} other {Only the reviewer of {card} checks its design or follow-up.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.messa.note: A refused card loop step (#1382, #1467): the agent isn't on the side of the loop the step belongs to (a reviewer posting a design or a follow-up, a builder answering its own). A follow-up: a change asked of reviewed work (such as a screenshot's), ready for the reviewer's check. {card} is a card key; side (select): builder or reviewer, whose step it is. Translate each sentence.

workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.next.text: {side, select, builder {Leave it to the card's builder; a reviewer answers with ok or gaps.} other {Leave it to the card's reviewer; nobody checks their own work.}}
workflow.refused.loop.stepNotYours.next.note: The next step after a refused card loop step from the wrong side (#1382, #1467). side: builder or reviewer, the agent the step belongs to. ok and gaps are the reviewer's answers, as agents name them: keep them as they are.

workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.change.text: How long is set in Project Settings → Card loops → Design check wait.
workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.change.note: Where the wait for a design check is changed (#1382). Names of settings: keep them as Combwork shows them.

workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.message.text: {card}: its design's check is due in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.message.note: A refused going ahead with a design before its reviewer's check is due (#1382, Card loops → Design check wait). {card} is a card key; {minutes} how many minutes are left.

workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.next.text: Wait for the answer; with none by then, go ahead as posted.
workflow.refused.loop.tooEarly.next.note: The next step after going ahead with a design too early (#1382).

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ch.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Who merges. A card keeps the rules it started with.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ch.note: Where the rule that Combwork merges cards is changed; a card keeps the rules it started under unless the change is applied to it.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.me.text: Combwork merges {card}: agents don't merge it or report its merge.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.me.note: A refused report of a merge, or a claim of the merge slot, for a card whose rules say Combwork merges it (the merge queue). {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.text: Once it is approved, the merge queue merges it and moves it to Done: wait for that, or for it to come back.
workflow.refused.merge.combworkMerges.ne.note: The next step after a refused merge of a card Combwork merges, when it isn't in the merge queue yet.

workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..text: {card} depends on {waitsFor}, which isn't Done: it isn't closed as merged before then.
workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..note: HI-2709: a refused report of a merge: the card depends on {waitsFor} (card keys, comma-joined), which aren't Done yet. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..text: Wait for {waitsFor} to be Done, then report the merge again.
workflow.refused.merge.waitsForBlockers..note: HI-2709: the next step after a merge report refused for an unfinished dependency: {waitsFor} are card keys.

workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.messag.text: {card} would be in {stage} with nobody on it{also, select, yes {, and the move skips: {rules}} other {}}.
workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.messag.note: A refused move into the Active stage by the Combwork Assistant (HI-2062): the card {card} (its key, like AM-12) would have no agent on it. {stage} is the stage's name. {also} (select): yes when the move also skips other rules, listed in {rules}; translate both branches.

workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.next.text: {reader, select, you {Choose nobody on it, an agent on it, or an agent started on it.} other {Ask the user which they want: nobody on it (move it again with override and their reason), an agent on it (agent), or an agent started on it (cw_start_task).}}
workflow.refused.move.doingNobody.next.note: The next step after the Assistant's move into Active was refused for leaving nobody on the card: the user chooses nobody on it, an agent given the card, or an agent started on it. override, agent and cw_start_task are names of a call's fields and a tool: keep them as they are. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan.text: {reader, select, you {These rules are set in Version Control, where you can change them.} other {These rules are set in Version Control, where the user can change them.}}
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.chan.note: Where the rules a move would skip are changed: the project's Version Control tab (a tab name: use it as Combwork shows it). {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.mess.note: A move that skips rules: {rules} lists the rule names.

workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.next.text: {reader, select, you {Moving it anyway needs your reason: one you gave for it, or one you give once told which rules this skips.} other {Move it anyway only with the user's reason. One they gave with their request is enough ("I merged it by hand", say): move it again with override and that reason, in their words. With none, tell them which rules this skips and ask for theirs.}}
workflow.refused.move.needsOverride.next.note: The next step for a move that skips rules (said to the Combwork Assistant): move anyway (an override) only with the user's own reason, given with the request (then the agent moves it at once, HI-2260) or after being told which rules the move skips. {reader} (select): you is the window's wording, other the agent's (the user named as the user); translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.move.noStage.change.text: A project's steps follow its options in Version Control.
workflow.refused.move.noStage.change.note: Where the stages a project has are set: its Version Control options (a tab name: use it as Combwork shows it).

workflow.refused.move.noStage.message.text: {card} can't go to {stage}: this project's rules have no such step.
workflow.refused.move.noStage.message.note: A refused move: the card was moved to a board stage the project's workflow rules don't have (Review with no review, say). {card} is a card key, {stage} a stage name.

workflow.refused.move.noStage.next.text: Move it to one of its steps: {stages}.
workflow.refused.move.noStage.next.note: The next step after a move to a stage the rules lack: the stages they have. {stages} lists stage names.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.messag.text: {card} is in {stage}: {move} isn't possible from there.
workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.messag.note: A refused intent: not possible from the stage the card is in. {stage} is a stage name, {move} the intent.

workflow.refused.move.notFromHere.next.note: The next step: the intents possible from the stage. {moves} lists them.

workflow.refused.move.useIntent.message.text: Agents don't move cards between columns.
workflow.refused.move.useIntent.message.note: A refused column move by an agent: agents act by intent.

workflow.refused.move.useIntent.next.note: The next step after a refused column move: {intent} is the intent to use.

workflow.refused.paths.excluded.message.text: {card}: {path} is in {folder}, which a project without version control leaves out of its work.
workflow.refused.paths.excluded.message.note: A refused declaration of a card's paths (#1511): in a project without version control (None), a card's paths are the files of its work; {path} is under {folder} (node_modules, .venv, .git, .combwork or a folder the project excludes), which never counts as work. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.paths.excluded.next.text: Declare only the files of the work, outside {folder}: a card's paths narrow the project's work, never widen it.
workflow.refused.paths.excluded.next.note: The next step after a refused declaration of a card's paths: name files outside the excluded folder {folder} (#1511).

workflow.refused.platform.changed.messag.text: {card} can't start under these rules: its project uses {platform} now.
workflow.refused.platform.changed.messag.note: HI-2799: a refused start: the start was prepared under the project’s previous version control, and the project was switched meanwhile. {card} is a card key; {platform} is None, Git or jj.

workflow.refused.platform.changed.next.text: Start it again: it is then checked under {platform}’s rules.
workflow.refused.platform.changed.next.note: HI-2799: the next step after a start refused because the project switched version control meanwhile. {platform} is None, Git or jj.

workflow.refused.platform.detachedFolder.text: {card} can’t start: the project folder is on no branch (its head is detached at {head}), so what its builder commits would be on none.
workflow.refused.platform.detachedFolder.note: HI-3104: a refused start in a Git project whose cards are built in the project folder: the folder has no branch checked out (a detached head, as a jj repository colocated with Git leaves it after switching back to Git), so commits made there would belong to no branch. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {head} a short commit id.

workflow.refused.platform.detachedFolder.text: {has, select, yes {Check out its branch in the project folder (git switch {branch}), then start it again.} other {Check out a branch in the project folder (an existing one with git switch, or a new one with git switch -c), then start it again.}}
workflow.refused.platform.detachedFolder.note: HI-3104: the next step after a start refused because the project folder is on no branch. has (select): yes when Combwork found the branch to check out ({branch}, its name), other when it found none it could name. git switch and git switch -c are commands: keep them as they are. Translate both whole sentences.

workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.mess.text: {why, select, tooLarge {{card}: jj left {count, plural, one {a new file} other {# new files}} out of its snapshot for being over its size limit for new files (snapshot.max-new-file-size), so the work isn't all recorded: {files}.} autoTrack {{card}: jj's setting snapshot.auto-track is {setting} here, not all(), so jj doesn't record new files by itself and the work may not all be recorded.} mergeWorkingCopy {{card}: the slot's working copy has more than one parent, so its work isn't one line of commits.} notFromBase {{card}: the work in its slot doesn't start from the card's base {base}.} otherCard {{card}: commit {commit} is {other}'s work.} divergent {{card}: commit {commit} is divergent in jj (its change has more than one visible commit).} conflicted {{card}: commit {commit} has unresolved conflicts.} tooLong {{card}: its work has more than {max, number} commits.} unbound {{card}: its slot isn't prepared for this card any more.} isolated {{card}: jj projects have no check copies yet.} recovered {{card}: commits of its work hold copies that Recover… wrote beside the original files: {files}.} other {{card}: jj refused it.}}
workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.mess.note: HI-2868: a refused move on a card of a project using jj (Jujutsu): why its work can't be taken as it is. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {commit} and {base} are short commit ids; {other} is another card's key; {max} is a number; {files} is a list of file paths and {count} their number (HI-2973). 'working copy', 'divergent' and 'snapshot' are jj's terms; snapshot.max-new-file-size is jj's setting: keep it as it is. Translate each sentence. autoTrack (HI-3096): the user's jj setting snapshot.auto-track ({setting}, its value) isn't all(), so jj leaves new files untracked; snapshot.auto-track and all() are jj's: keep them. recovered (HI-2996): Recover… (a button of a stale slot, as the window names it) wrote a copy of the user's version beside a file that had changed meanwhile, and commits of the card's work hold that copy; {files} is a list of file paths, as they are.

workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.next.text: {why, select, tooLarge {Leave a file out deliberately with .gitignore, or raise jj's limit (jj config set --repo snapshot.max-new-file-size and a size in bytes) and commit it with jj commit, then submit again.} autoTrack {Set it back to all() for this repository (jj config set --repo snapshot.auto-track 'all()'), then submit again: jj then records the new files.} mergeWorkingCopy {Commit the work with jj commit, so the working copy is empty on one parent, then submit again.} notFromBase {Rebase the work onto the card's base, or start the card again.} otherCard {Leave that card's commits out of this card's work (rebase without them), then submit again.} divergent {Resolve the divergence in jj (abandon or rewrite one side), then try again.} conflicted {Resolve the conflicts in jj, then try again.} tooLong {Squash some of the commits, then submit again.} unbound {Put the card back and start it again.} isolated {Run the check again without --isolated, in the card's slot.} recovered {Compare each copy with its original and keep what you want under the original name, then take the copies out of every commit of the work (jj squash or jj diffedit: deleting them in a later commit leaves them in its history) and submit again.} other {Look at the slot with jj, then try again.}}
workflow.refused.platform.jjRefused.next.note: HI-2868: the next step after a refused move on a jj project's card, by the reason (why, select). jj commit, --isolated, .gitignore, jj config set --repo snapshot.max-new-file-size and jj config set --repo snapshot.auto-track 'all()' are commands and names: keep them as they are. 'working copy' and 'divergent' are jj's terms. Translate each sentence. recovered (HI-2996): copies Recover… wrote beside the originals are in commits of the card's work: the user's version of each is compared with the original, kept under the original name if wanted, and the copies taken out of every commit (jj squash and jj diffedit are commands: keep them).

workflow.refused.platform.keptAcross.mes.text: {card} can't start: its committed work from before it was put back is kept in slot {slot}, a {platform} slot from before the repository switched to {now}.
workflow.refused.platform.keptAcross.mes.note: HI-3069: a refused start: the card was put back with commits under one version control, kept for it in its slot, and the repository has since switched to the other, so that slot can’t be lent back and the card would start without its work. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {slot} a slot’s name; {platform} and {now} are Git or jj (keep them).

workflow.refused.platform.keptAcross.nex.text: {gone, select, yes {Its folder is gone, so nothing of it is left to go on with: remove the slot (Version Control → Slots and copies, Remove…), and {card} starts afresh from its target.} other {Switch the repository back to {platform} to go on with {card} in that slot.}}
workflow.refused.platform.keptAcross.nex.note: HI-3069: the next step after a start refused because the card’s kept slot is of the other version control. gone (select): yes when the slot’s folder was deleted, so removing the slot lets the card start afresh; other: switching back is the way on. Version Control, Slots and copies and Remove… are names in the window: as translated there. {platform} is Git or jj; {card} a card key.

workflow.refused.platform.keptElsewhere..text: {card} can't start there: its committed work from before it was put back is kept in slot {slot}, and it starts only in that slot.
workflow.refused.platform.keptElsewhere..note: HI-3132: a refused start: the card was put back with commits, kept for it in slot {slot} (a name), and this start would have put it somewhere else (the project folder, or across a wait for that slot), without that work. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.platform.keptElsewhere..text: Wait until {slot} is free, then start {card} again: it gets that slot back, with its work.
workflow.refused.platform.keptElsewhere..note: HI-3132: the next step after that refusal: once the slot {slot} is free (nothing works in it), starting the card {card} again lends it that slot with the work kept in it.

workflow.refused.platform.keptLine.messa.text: {card} can’t start: its branch was made from {kept} and still holds history {target} lacks, but its lane merges into {target}.
workflow.refused.platform.keptLine.messa.note: HI-3112: a refused start: the card was started before, put back, and its branch (made from {kept}, the branch it merged into then) is kept, so it keeps merging into {kept}; but the card is in a lane whose cards merge into {target}. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {kept} and {target} are branch names.

workflow.refused.platform.keptLine.next.text: Take it out of the lane and start it on its own, to merge into {kept}; or make a new card for {target}.
workflow.refused.platform.keptLine.next.note: HI-3112: the next step after a start refused because the card’s kept branch ({kept}) isn’t its lane’s ({target}). {kept} and {target} are branch names.

workflow.refused.platform.noTarget.messa.text: {card} can’t start: its project has no target bookmark chosen, the one its work merges into.
workflow.refused.platform.noTarget.messa.note: HI-3106: a refused start in a project using jj (Jujutsu): no target bookmark (Work merges into) is chosen, and jj has no default to fall back on, as Git has its default branch. {card} is a card key like AM-12. A bookmark is jj’s name for a branch.

workflow.refused.platform.noTarget.next.text: Choose one in Version Control → Workflow (Work merges into), then start it again.
workflow.refused.platform.noTarget.next.note: HI-3106: the next step after a start refused for no target bookmark: the user chooses it in the window. Version Control, Workflow and Work merges into are names in the window: as translated there.

workflow.refused.platform.noUpstream.mes.text: {card} can’t start: {target} tracks no remote branch, and with “The target branch follows its remote” on each card starts from its remote.
workflow.refused.platform.noUpstream.mes.note: HI-3128: a refused start under the workflow option “The target branch follows its remote” (its name: use its words): the branch work merges into ({target}) has no upstream, as a new version’s branch made by Start the next version has, so there is no remote head to start from. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.platform.noUpstream.nex.text: {how, select, ready {If {remote} hasn’t got {target} yet, publish it there: {publish}. If it has, set what {target} tracks: {track1}, then {track2}. Then start it again; or turn off “The target branch follows its remote”.} choose {This repository has no remote, or several, that Combwork can name: in these commands {remote} stands for the one {target} should follow. If it hasn’t got {target} yet, publish it there: {publish}. If it has, set what {target} tracks: {track1}, then {track2}. Then start it again; or turn off “The target branch follows its remote”.} shallow {This repository is a shallow clone, which follow mode can’t use: fetch its whole history (git fetch --unshallow), then publish {target} or set what it tracks, and start it again; or turn off “The target branch follows its remote”.} other {The remote {target} would follow ({remote}) has several push addresses, or none, and follow mode publishes to exactly one: leave it one, then publish {target} or set what it tracks, and start it again; or turn off “The target branch follows its remote”.}}
workflow.refused.platform.noUpstream.nex.note: HI-3128: the next step after a start refused for a target with no upstream under “The target branch follows its remote” (its name: use its words). how (select, keep the keys): ready, a remote Combwork can name ({remote}); choose, none it can name ({remote} is then a placeholder such as <remote>, which the user replaces); shallow, the repository is a shallow clone; other, the named remote ({remote}) has several push addresses or none. {publish}, {track1}, {track2} are git commands: keep them exactly as they are. Combwork runs none of them: the user does.

workflow.refused.platform.offLine.messag.text: {card}'s folder isn't on its branch {line}: {where, select, detached {its head is detached at {head}} other {it is on {on}}}, so the work there isn't what the card would merge.
workflow.refused.platform.offLine.messag.note: HI-3010: a refused submit: the card's slot (its folder) has another branch or no branch checked out (a detached head), so its commits there aren't on the card's own branch, which is what review and the merge read. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {line} and {on} are branch names; {head} is a short commit id. Translate each branch of the select.

workflow.refused.platform.offLine.next.text: {where, select, detached {Put the commits on the card's branch: git switch -c {lineArg} if it doesn't exist yet, else git switch {lineArg} and git cherry-pick the commits made off it. Then submit again.} other {{made, select, no {The card's branch doesn't exist yet: make it from where the card started with git switch -c {lineArg} {start}, then git cherry-pick there the card's own commits made on {onArg}. Then submit again.} other {Switch back with git switch {lineArg}, and git cherry-pick there any commits of the card's made on {onArg}. Then submit again.}}}}
workflow.refused.platform.offLine.next.note: HI-3010, HI-3116: the next step after a submit refused because the card’s folder isn’t on its branch, by where it is (where, select: a detached head, or another branch) and, on another branch, whether the card’s branch exists yet (made, select: no, or yes). git switch -c, git switch and git cherry-pick are commands: keep them and their arguments exactly as they are. {lineArg} and {onArg} are branch names as typed in a shell (possibly in quotes); {start} is a commit id.

workflow.refused.platform.slotLeft.messa.text: {unknown, select, yes {Combwork couldn't tell whether {card}'s slot {slot} ({folder}) is still the card's, so it wasn't submitted.} other {{card}'s slot {slot} ({folder}) isn't the card's any more: Combwork ended its lease there, so the work in that folder may be another card's now.}}
workflow.refused.platform.slotLeft.messa.note: HI-3118: a refused submit: the card was started in a slot (a working folder Combwork lends to one card or lane at a time), and Combwork no longer holds that slot for it (its lane ended, say), so the folder may have been lent to another card since. unknown yes: whether it still holds it couldn't be read. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {slot} a slot's name like slot-a; {folder} its path. Translate each branch of the select.

workflow.refused.platform.slotLeft.next.text: {unknown, select, yes {Try again in a moment.} other {Put the card back and start it again: it gets a slot of its own, with its committed work if the slot was kept for it.}}
workflow.refused.platform.slotLeft.next.note: HI-3118: the next step after a submit refused because the card’s slot is no longer held for it (unknown yes: that couldn’t be read). Put back and start are actions on the card.

workflow.refused.platform.switching.mess.text: {card} can't start now: its repository's version control is being switched.
workflow.refused.platform.switching.mess.note: HI-2799: a refused start: the project’s repository is switching between Git and jj, and nothing starts on it meanwhile. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.platform.switching.next.text: Try again in a moment, once the switch has finished.
workflow.refused.platform.switching.next.note: HI-2799: the next step after a start refused while the repository’s version control is switched.

workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.mes.text: {card} was started on {target}, which no longer exists in this repository.
workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.mes.note: HI-2753: a refused move (a submit): the branch the card was started on and merges into (its target, {target}) was deleted, as an integration branch is once it has been merged. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.nex.text: The user or the Assistant can move it to another branch with its work kept: set its Merges into, or retarget Work merges into.
workflow.refused.platform.targetGone.nex.note: HI-2753: the next step when the branch a card started on is gone: the user or the Combwork Assistant moves the card to another branch (its Merges into, or a retarget after changing Work merges into). Merges into and Work merges into are names in the window: as translated there.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.messag.text: {card}: Combwork couldn't read {what}, so the rule {rule} can't be checked.
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.messag.note: A refused move: a fact a rule needs could not be read (git missing, folder gone). {what} says what, {rule} the rule id.

workflow.refused.platform.unknown.next.text: Check Provider Setup or the folder, then try again.
workflow.refused.platform.unknown.next.note: The next step when Combwork could not read what a rule needs.

workflow.refused.queue.advancing.message.text: {card} is being merged into {target} now: it can no longer be taken out of the merge queue.
workflow.refused.queue.advancing.message.note: A refused Remove from queue: the merge queue has begun moving the target to the card's merge (it finishes even after a restart). {card} is a card key, {target} a branch name.

workflow.refused.queue.advancing.next.text: Wait for the merge to finish. If the change isn't wanted, revert it in {target}.
workflow.refused.queue.advancing.next.note: The next step after a refused Remove from queue while the card is being merged. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.change.text: Retry merge on the merge queue retries it once.
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.change.note: Who can override a refused requeue: the user, with Retry merge on the merge queue (glossary 2.5: merge queue).

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.message.text: {card} at {revision} can't go back into the merge queue unchanged: {why}
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.message.note: A refused resubmission into the merge queue. {card} is a card key, {revision} a short revision id, {why} one of the requeue reasons below, a whole sentence.

workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.next.text: Fix the failure, commit and submit the new revision.
workflow.refused.requeue.allowed.next.note: The next step after a refused unchanged requeue.

workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.text: {card} has a decision you haven't read.
workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.note: A refused review or verdict: the card has a newer decision than the reviewer has received.

workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.text: Read it, judge whether the work meets it, then give your verdict.
workflow.refused.review.decisionsReceive.note: The next step after a refused verdict for an unread decision.

workflow.refused.review.headMoved.messag.text: {card}'s line has moved since it was submitted: it was submitted at {submitted}, and its head is now {head}, a different change. A pass covers only the revision submitted.
workflow.refused.review.headMoved.messag.note: A refused passing verdict (HI-1763): the card's branch has new commits since the revision under review (a follow-up, say). {card} is the card's key; {submitted} and {head} are commits' short hashes.

workflow.refused.review.headMoved.next.text: A commit you asked for: ask its builder to submit {head} as a follow-up (cw_request_builder), which keeps it in Review with no round counted, then start your review again. Otherwise give a failing verdict saying so (cw_verdict, pass: false), and its builder submits it as the next round.
workflow.refused.review.headMoved.next.note: The next step after a pass refused because the branch moved on (HI-1763, HI-1832): a commit the reviewer asked for is submitted by the builder as a follow-up (the card stays in Review, no round counted) and reviewed again; any other is failed so the builder submits it as a new round. {head} is a commit's short hash; keep the tool names and the argument as they are.

workflow.refused.review.inProgress.chang.text: Only the user takes a review over; one whose reviewer has left the project or stopped is free again.
workflow.refused.review.inProgress.chang.note: Who can take over a review in progress (HI-2487): only the user; it is free again once its reviewer agent is removed from the project or its session has stopped.

workflow.refused.review.inProgress.messa.text: {who, select, user {The user is reviewing {card}'s submission {submission}} other {{reviewer} is reviewing {card}'s submission {submission}}}, and has been for {minutes, plural, =0 {less than a minute} one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
