workflow.refused.review.inProgress.messa.note: A refused start of a review (HI-2487): someone else started reviewing the same submission and hasn't given its verdict. {who}: user (the user reviews it) or agent (another reviewer agent, named by {reviewer}, its name). {card} is a card key like AM-12, {submission} the submission's number, {minutes} how long ago its review started (select: translate each branch).

workflow.refused.review.inProgress.next.text: {who, select, user {Leave it to the user} other {Leave it to {reviewer}}}: don't review {card} or give it a verdict.
workflow.refused.review.inProgress.next.note: The next step after a review refused because someone else is reviewing the card (HI-2487). {who}: user (the user reviews it) or agent (another reviewer agent, named by {reviewer}). {card} is a card key (select: translate each branch).

workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.mes.note: A refused review: the card has no submission.

workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.nex.text: Wait for its builder to submit it.
workflow.refused.review.noSubmission.nex.note: The next step when there is nothing to review.

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.change.text: Only Move anyway, on the card, skips this rule.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.change.note: Who can override the no-self-review rule: only the user, moving the card anyway (glossary 2.4: override, Move anyway).

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.messag.text: You worked on {card}, so you can't review it.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.messag.note: A refused review: the reviewer is one of the agents who built the card.

workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.next.text: Leave the review to another reviewer.
workflow.refused.review.notAuthor.next.note: The next step after a refused self-review.

workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged.
workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.note: Where the rule that refused starting a card before the cards it waits for are done is changed.
A refused start of a card. {card} and {waitsFor} are card keys (AM-12): the card waits for {waitsFor}'s work to be merged or accepted.

workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.text: Wait for {waitsFor} to be done, or work on another card.
workflow.refused.start.dependenciesInteg.note: The next step after a refused start: {waitsFor} is the card key it waits for.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.change.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done.
workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.change.note: Where the rule that refused starting a blocked card is changed.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.messag.note: A refused start of a card. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {reason} is why the card is blocked, in the words given.

workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.next.text: Wait for it to be unblocked, or work on another card.
workflow.refused.start.notBlocked.next.note: The next step after a refused start of a blocked card.

workflow.refused.start.platformReady.mes.text: {card} can't start: cards don't run in a jj project yet.
workflow.refused.start.platformReady.mes.note: A refused start of a card in a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): Combwork shows its repository but doesn’t start card work there yet. {card} is a card key. Keep jj (the tool’s name).

workflow.refused.start.platformReady.nex.text: Work on it outside Combwork’s cards, or switch the project to Git in Version Control.
workflow.refused.start.platformReady.nex.note: The next step after a refused start in a jj project (HI-2799). Version Control is the tab’s name (glossary 2.1). Keep Git and jj.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.cha.text: This is set in Version Control → Where cards are built.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.cha.note: Where the rule that refused starting for want of a slot is changed.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.mes.text: {card} can't start: no slot is free.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.mes.note: A refused start: every working folder (slot) is lent to other work. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.nex.text: Wait for a slot to be free.
workflow.refused.start.slotAvailable.nex.note: The next step after a refused start for want of a slot.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.cha.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Checks pass before review.
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.cha.note: Where the rule that refused a submit for a missing check is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.mes.text: Review refused: {check} hasn't passed on {revision}.{why, select, notCheck { Its last run passed but didn't count: it wasn't the check's configured command.} notContained { Its last run passed but didn't count: what it ran on doesn't contain the revision.} dirty { Its last run passed but didn't count: the folder had uncommitted changes{files, select, none {} other { ({files})}}.} moved { Its last run passed but didn't count: something else was checked out by its end.} changed { Its last run passed but didn't count: files changed in the folder while it ran{files, select, none {} other { ({files})}}.} revisionChanged { Its last run passed but didn't count: the card's files changed while it ran.} other {}}
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.mes.note: A refused submit: a configured check has no passing counted run on the revision. {check} is the check name, {revision} a short revision id. {why} picks why its last run there didn't count (#1654; keep each branch's key as it is; 'other': it didn't run there, or failed, and nothing is added); {files} lists the paths that changed, or is 'none' (keep the key).

workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.nex.text: {why, select, dirty {Commit or remove the uncommitted changes, run {command} again, then submit again.} changed {{copy, select, yes {Run {command} again with nothing else writing in the folder, or add --isolated to run it in a check copy of its own, then submit again.} other {Run {command} again with nothing else writing in the folder, then submit again.}}} notContained {Run {command} in the card's own folder, at its revision, then submit again.} other {Run {command}, then submit again.}}
workflow.refused.submit.checksPassed.nex.note: The next step after a refused submit for a missing check: {command} is the command to run. {why} picks the remedy for why its last run didn't count (#1654; keep each branch's key as it is); {copy} is 'yes' where a check copy (--isolated, kept as typed) can be used.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.change.text: This rule comes with review and merging in Version Control.
workflow.refused.submit.clean.change.note: Where the rule that refused a submit with uncommitted changes comes from.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.message.text: {card} can't go to review: {folder} has uncommitted changes ({files}).
workflow.refused.submit.clean.message.note: A refused submit: the working folder has uncommitted changes. {folder} is a folder path, {files} a list of file paths.

workflow.refused.submit.clean.next.text: Commit the card's changes, then submit for review again; if you were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing. Changes that aren't the card's: ask before removing them.
workflow.refused.submit.clean.next.note: The next step after a refused submit for review with uncommitted changes (HI-1618, HI-2227, HI-2257): an agent doing the card commits its work; one asked only to submit it asks the user before committing; changes that aren't the card's are removed only once asked about.

workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.text: {card} has a decision or a comment from the user that you haven't seen.
workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.note: A refused submit (HI-2854): the card has a decision, or a comment the user wrote, newer than the builder has received.

workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.text: Check your work against each (listed below, or read the card), then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.decisionsReceive.note: The next step after a refused submit for an unseen decision or comment of the user's: the agent's reply lists them below when it can.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.message.note: A refused submit for review: the card's line has no commit since it started (git's words: nothing committed). {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.submit.empty.next.text: {changes, select, yes {Commit the card's work, then submit for review again; if you were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing.} none {Its folder has no changes either. A card that needs none (it only runs or checks something, or its work is already there) is no-code: ask for that with cw_ask_user (action noCode), or cw_ask_assistant where it's already decided. Otherwise make its change, commit it and submit again.} other {Commit the card's work, then submit for review again; if you were asked only to submit it (not to do the card), ask the user before committing. A card that needs no change is no-code: ask for that with cw_ask_user (action noCode).}}
workflow.refused.submit.empty.next.note: The next step after a refused submit for review with nothing committed (HI-2227, HI-2257). {changes} (select): yes when the card's folder has uncommitted changes (an agent doing the card commits them; one asked only to submit it asks the user first), none when it has none (a card needing no change is made no-code by the user, asked with the tools named), other when unknown. cw_ask_user, cw_ask_assistant and noCode are names of tools and an option: keep them as they are; translate each branch's whole sentences.

workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ch.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Each card’s focused tests.
workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ch.note: Where the rule that refused a submit for focused tests (G20) is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.me.text: Review refused: {card}'s focused tests couldn't be chosen for {revision}: {state, select, tooBroad {its project's picker says the change needs every test.} other {{why, select, noPicker {the project has no picker.} timedOut {its project's picker took too long.} badOutput {its project's picker gave output Combwork can't read.} tooMany {its project's picker named too many tests.} moved {its folder moved to another revision while the picker ran.} dirty {its folder had uncommitted changes.} changed {files changed in its folder while the picker ran.} noChange {its change couldn't be read.} other {its project's picker failed.}}}}
workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.me.note: A refused submit (G20, HI-1367): the tests the card's change needs couldn't be chosen. {card} is its key, {revision} a short commit id; {state} and {why} pick the reason (keep each branch's key as it is).

workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ne.text: Name the tests the change needs with tests on submit, for the reviewer to check, or fix what stopped the picker, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.focusedChosen.ne.note: The next step after a refused submit for focused tests (G20), addressed to the agent: tests is the submit tool’s argument, kept as typed.

workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.text: {card}'s follow-up is its builder's to submit: you aren't building it.
workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.note: A refused follow-up submission (HI-1832: a commit its reviewer asked for, submitted while the card is in Review): only the agent building the card submits one. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.text: Leave it to its builder, or say what you found in a comment.
workflow.refused.submit.followUpNotBuild.note: The next step after a follow-up submission refused because the agent is not the card's builder (HI-1832).

workflow.refused.submit.identity.change.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Commits use the project's identity.
workflow.refused.submit.identity.change.note: Where the identity rule is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.message.text: {missing, select, yes {{card} can't be submitted: its commits must use the project's identity, and git has none set for the project.} other {{card}: commit {commit} isn't authored with the project's identity ({email}).}}
workflow.refused.submit.identity.message.note: A refused submit: a commit's author email isn't the project's, as git config has it now. {missing} (select; keep the keys): yes when git has no identity (name and email) for the project at all. {commit} is a short commit id, {email} the project's email address.

workflow.refused.submit.identity.next.text: {missing, select, yes {Set the project's identity in Version Control → Branches & remotes → Commit identity (or with {command}), then submit again.} other {Set the identity, run {command}, then submit again.}}
workflow.refused.submit.identity.next.note: The next step after a refused submit for a commit's identity: {command} is the git command to use (kept as typed). {missing} (select; keep the keys): yes when git has no identity for the project; Version Control → Branches & remotes → Commit identity is where Combwork's window sets it (use the names Combwork shows for the tab, its section and heading).

workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.mes.text: {card} is already submitted at {revision} and waits for review or merging.
workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.mes.note: A refused submit: the same revision is already waiting. {card} is a card key, {revision} a short revision id.

workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.nex.text: Wait for its review or merge.
workflow.refused.submit.notDuplicate.nex.note: The next step after a refused duplicate submission.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.c.text: This rule is set in Version Control → Agents stop what they started before review.
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.c.note: Where the rule about stopping runs before review is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.m.text: {card}: runs you started are still going ({runs}).
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.m.note: A refused submit: the agent still has runs going. {runs} lists their titles.

workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.n.text: Stop them or let them finish, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.ownRunsStopped.n.note: The next step after a refused submit while runs are going.

workflow.refused.submit.ready.message.note: A refused submit: the revision stores conflicts. {files} lists file paths.

workflow.refused.submit.ready.next.text: Resolve the conflicts, then submit again.
workflow.refused.submit.ready.next.note: The next step after a refused submit of a conflicted revision.

workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.note: A refused submit: the same revision again without a note.

workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.text: Submit it again with a note saying what changed in your answer, or commit a new revision.
workflow.refused.submit.sameRevisionNote.note: The next step when submitting a reviewed revision again.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.change.text: Each card in its own folder needs no trailers: Version Control → Where cards are built.
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.change.note: Where the setting that needs commit trailers is changed.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.message.text: {card}: commit {commit} has no card trailer, and another card's agent works in this folder.
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.message.note: A refused submit in a shared folder: a commit lacks the Combwork-Card trailer. {commit} is a short commit id.

workflow.refused.submit.trailer.next.text: {at, select, head {Run {command}, then submit again.} other {Other commits follow it, so amending or rebasing would rewrite them, other agents' work among them: do neither. Report it with cw_cannot_within_rules (rule submit.trailer), and the user decides.}}
workflow.refused.submit.trailer.next.note: The next step after a refused submit for a missing trailer (HI-2562). {at} (select): head when the commit is the folder's newest, so amending it is safe; other when commits follow it. {command} is the git command to run, kept as typed; cw_cannot_within_rules is a tool's name, kept as typed.

workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.messag.text: {card}: its files haven't changed since it started.
workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.messag.note: A refused submit for review in a project with no version control: none of the card's files changed. {card} is a card key.

workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.next.text: Change the card's files, then submit it for review.
workflow.refused.submit.unchanged.next.note: The next step after a refused submit for review in a project with no version control, nothing changed.

workflow.refused.verdict.currentSubmissi.note: A refused verdict: it names an older submission. {submission} is its number.
The next step after a verdict on an old submission: {latest} is the latest submission number.

workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.messa.text: You haven't started a review of {card}'s submission {submission}.
workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.messa.note: A refused verdict: the reviewer never started reviewing that submission. {submission} is its number.

workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.next.text: Start the review first, then give your verdict.
workflow.refused.verdict.reviewing.next.note: The next step after a verdict without a started review.

workflow.refused.why.passes.text: {n, number} of {q, plural, one {# reviewer} other {# reviewers}} passed it.
workflow.refused.why.passes.note: The {why} of a refused merge: not enough distinct reviewers passed the revision. {n} and {q} are numbers.

workflow.refused.why.requeueLimit.text: it was sent back unchanged {n, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} already.
workflow.refused.why.requeueLimit.note: The {why} of a refused requeue: the limit of unchanged requeues was reached. {n} is how many.

workflow.refused.why.requeueNotTransient.text: its last merge failed for a reason in the work (a conflict, red checks or a hook), which needs a new revision.
workflow.refused.why.requeueNotTransient.note: The {why} of a refused requeue: the merge failure wasn't transient. Starts lower case: it follows a colon.

workflow.refused.why.stale.note: The {why} of a refused merge or requeue: the revision's pass no longer holds.

workflow.refused.why.userOk.text: it waits for the OK before merging.
workflow.refused.why.userOk.note: The {why} of a refused merge: the user's approval is missing.

workflow.roundChoice.text: {choice, select, carryOn {Carry on} split {Split it} accept {Accept with follow-ups} takeOver {Take it over} other {{choice}}}
workflow.roundChoice.note: One of the user's four choices when a card reaches its card loop's round limit: carry on with more review rounds, split the card into smaller ones, accept the work as it is with follow-up cards, or take the work over themselves. Translate each choice; keep the codes before the braces.

workflow.rule.approval.given.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G10).

workflow.rule.card.kind.text: A card's kind is set when it is made
workflow.rule.card.kind.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a change skips it: a card is code or no code (a decision, a write-up, a trial) from when it is made; changing it later is an exception the user makes (glossary: override).

workflow.rule.done.contained.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: a card is done only when its work is in its target (glossary 2.6: G5).

workflow.rule.forward.resolutionSource.text: A resolution merges the commit it resolves
workflow.rule.forward.resolutionSource.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move can’t check it (HI-2999): a card made by Resolve on a builder (it merges one branch into another by hand) must contain, merged, the commit that came back from the merge queue, not a copy of its changes.

workflow.rule.integrate.approved.text: Work is reviewed before it's merged
workflow.rule.integrate.approved.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G1).

workflow.rule.integrate.checksPassed.text: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.rule.integrate.checksPassed.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G9).

workflow.rule.integrate.upToDate.text: Work is up to date before it merges
workflow.rule.integrate.upToDate.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G8, without the branch name).

workflow.rule.move.doingNobody.text: A card in Active has someone on it, unless you say otherwise
workflow.rule.move.doingNobody.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips it (HI-2062): the Combwork Assistant moves a card into Active with nobody on it only with the user's reason (glossary: override). Active is a stage's name.

workflow.rule.requeue.allowed.text: Unchanged work is queued again only after a failure outside it
workflow.rule.requeue.allowed.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: work goes back into the merge queue unchanged only after a merge failed for a reason outside the work (a network error, a timeout).

workflow.rule.review.decisionsReceived.text: The reviewer has read every decision
workflow.rule.review.decisionsReceived.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.5: reviewer).

workflow.rule.review.inProgress.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move can't check it (HI-2487): a reviewer agent doesn't start a review another reviewer is still doing; only the user takes one over.

workflow.rule.review.notAuthor.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N2, G2).

workflow.rule.start.dependenciesIntegrat.text: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.rule.start.dependenciesIntegrat.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N6, G14).

workflow.rule.start.notBlocked.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.start.platformReady.text: Cards run only where Combwork supports the version control
workflow.rule.start.platformReady.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can’t check it (HI-2799): cards don’t start in a project using jj (Jujutsu) yet.

workflow.rule.start.slotAvailable.text: Each card in its own folder
workflow.rule.start.slotAvailable.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G11 values): a card starts only when a folder is free.

workflow.rule.submit.checksPassed.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: N3, G3).

workflow.rule.submit.clean.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.submit.decisionsReceived.text: The builder has seen every decision and every comment of the user's
workflow.rule.submit.decisionsReceived.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: the agent who built the card has seen every decision on it, and every comment the user wrote (HI-2854; glossary 2.5: builder).

workflow.rule.submit.focusedChosen.text: Each card’s focused tests are chosen before review
workflow.rule.submit.focusedChosen.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can’t check it (G20, HI-1367): the tests a card’s change needs are chosen, or named by its builder, when it is submitted.

workflow.rule.submit.identity.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G12).

workflow.rule.submit.notDuplicate.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: the same revision isn't submitted twice.

workflow.rule.submit.ownRunsStopped.text: Agents stop what they started before review
workflow.rule.submit.ownRunsStopped.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.6: G13).

workflow.rule.submit.ready.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it.

workflow.rule.submit.trailer.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: in a shared folder, each commit names its card.

workflow.rule.verdict.currentSubmission.text: A verdict is on the latest submission
workflow.rule.verdict.currentSubmission.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.rule.verdict.reviewing.note: A rule of the workflow, named where a move skips or can't check it: a reviewer starts a review before giving a verdict (glossary 2.3: verdict).

workflow.stage.active.note: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Active, was Doing): cards being worked on.

workflow.stage.approved.note: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Approved, was Passed): cards whose work passed review (or your OK) and isn’t merged yet.

workflow.stage.done.note: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Done): cards whose work is merged, or accepted.

workflow.stage.hold.note: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: On Hold): parked cards nobody picks up until the user moves them on.

workflow.stage.merging.note: A stage of the board inside Approved (glossary 2.2: Merging): cards in Combwork's merge queue.

workflow.stage.review.note: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Review): cards waiting for, or in, review.

workflow.stage.todo.note: A stage of the board (glossary 2.2: Todo): cards not started.

workflow.stageName.control.text: The name of {stage} has a character that can’t be shown (a line break or a tab).
workflow.stageName.control.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a stage’s name has a control character. {stage} is the stage’s default name (glossary 2.2).

workflow.stageName.duplicate.text: The name of {stage} is already another stage’s name.
workflow.stageName.duplicate.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: two stages would have the same name. {stage} is the default name of the stage renamed (glossary 2.2).

workflow.stageName.empty.text: The name of {stage} can’t be empty: remove it to use the default name.
workflow.stageName.empty.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a stage was given an empty name. {stage} is the stage’s default name (glossary 2.2).

workflow.stageName.long.text: The name of {stage} is longer than {max, number} characters.
workflow.stageName.long.note: Why workflow options cannot be saved: a stage’s name is too long. {stage} is the stage’s default name (glossary 2.2), {max} the most characters it takes.

workflow.unreadable.branch.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.branchedOff.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commit two lines of work have in common. {a} and {b} are commit ids or branch names.

workflow.unreadable.branchedOffTarget.text: where the work branched off its target
workflow.unreadable.branchedOffTarget.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commit the card's work and the branch it merges into have in common.

workflow.unreadable.cardPathsFiles.text: the card's paths: they hold over {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
workflow.unreadable.cardPathsFiles.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files a card names hold too many files. {n} is the limit.

workflow.unreadable.cardPathsSize.text: the card's paths: they hold over {n, number} GB
workflow.unreadable.cardPathsSize.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files a card names are too large. {n} is a size in gigabytes (GB, of 1024 MB): write the unit as your language does.

workflow.unreadable.change.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (glossary 2.3: change). {from} and {to} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.changeFingerprint.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": what tells a change apart from others (glossary 2.3: change).

workflow.unreadable.commitsOf.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {range} is a Git range of commits, like a1b2c3d..e4f5a6b.

workflow.unreadable.commitsOn.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {target} is a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.commitsSince.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {revision} and {base} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.contains.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {revision} and {target} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.defaultBranch.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the branch work merges into by default. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.deliverables.text: the work in {project}: it has over {n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
workflow.unreadable.deliverables.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a project without version control has too many files to read its work. {project} is a project name, {n} the limit.

workflow.unreadable.files.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files as they are at a revision. {revision} is a commit id or name.

workflow.unreadable.filesChanged.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {from} and {to} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.folderFor.note: What Combwork couldn't make, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a working folder (a Git worktree) for a branch. {branch} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.gitFolder.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the repository's .git folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.head.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commit checked out in a folder, or at the tip of a branch. {where} is a folder path or a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.history.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the commits of a branch. {target} is a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.holdsChange.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": whether the card's change is already in a commit or branch (glossary 2.3: change). {where} is a short commit id or a branch name.

workflow.unreadable.ignored.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the files Git is told to leave out. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.line.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a Git branch. {branch} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.pathOutside.text: the path {path}, which is outside the project
workflow.unreadable.pathOutside.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": a card's path that isn't in its project. {path} is the path.

workflow.unreadable.remoteBehind.text: where to start from: {target} has commits that {endpoint} doesn’t (push or pull them first)
workflow.unreadable.remoteBehind.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-1183): the local branch {target} has commits the remote branch it follows (at {endpoint}, an address) lacks, so Combwork won't start a card's work from either.

workflow.unreadable.remoteHead.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-1183): fetching the remote branch {branch} from {endpoint} (a remote's address) failed; {target} is the local branch that follows it. Git's own words follow.

workflow.unreadable.remoteSetup.text: the remote branch {target} follows (it must track one, on a remote with a single push address)
workflow.unreadable.remoteSetup.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-1183, “The target branch follows its remote”): the branch on a remote that the target branch {target} tracks; it tracks none, or its remote has several push addresses or none.

workflow.unreadable.replay.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the result of applying a revision's change onto another commit. {revision} and {onto} are short commit ids.

workflow.unreadable.replayedFiles.text: the files of the change applied again
workflow.unreadable.replayedFiles.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the result of applying the change again on another commit, to tell whether two revisions are the same change.

workflow.unreadable.reviewers.text: whether the reviewers of {card} are still running
workflow.unreadable.reviewers.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (HI-2487): which of the agents reviewing the card are still in the project with their sessions running. {card} is a card key like AM-12.

workflow.unreadable.revision.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …" (glossary 2.3: revision). {revision} is a commit id or name.

workflow.unreadable.revisionIn.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the revision checked out in a folder (glossary 2.3: revision). {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.state.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": whether a merge or rebase is going on in the folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.target.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the branch the work merges into. {target} is its name.

workflow.unreadable.tracking.text: which remote branch {branch} tracks (its upstream must be a branch on a remote, or it must track none)
workflow.unreadable.tracking.note: What Combwork couldn’t read, the object of "Combwork couldn’t read …" (HI-3126, “The target branch follows its remote”): how the branch {branch} tracks a remote branch. Its Git settings name only half of one, another local branch, or a remote that isn’t there, or they couldn’t be read.

workflow.unreadable.uncommitted.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …". {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.unreadable.worktrees.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": the Git worktrees of a repository. {folder} is its folder path.

workflow.unreadable.writes.note: What Combwork couldn't read, the object of "Combwork couldn't read …": which files changed in a folder. {folder} is a folder path.

workflow.value.commitMessage.branch.text: The branch’s own, with no card key or trailers
workflow.value.commitMessage.branch.note: A value of the workflow option “Commit message” (glossary 2.6, G19): the commit takes the message the branch’s commits have (with several, the first one’s subject and each one’s message), never the card’s key or Combwork’s trailers. Trailers: git’s “Key: value” lines at a message’s end.

workflow.value.commitMessage.cw.text: Combwork’s: the card’s key and title, with trailers
workflow.value.commitMessage.cw.note: A value of the workflow option “Commit message” (glossary 2.6, G19): the commit is titled with the card’s key and title (HI-12: Fix the login) and ends with Combwork’s trailers (Combwork-Card: HI-12 and others). Trailers: git’s “Key: value” lines at a message’s end.

workflow.value.finish.agentMerges.note: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.combworkMerges.note: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.committed.note: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.notChecked.note: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5).

workflow.value.finish.userIntegrates.note: A value of the workflow option “Who merges” (glossary 2.6, G5) for a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): Combwork never merges under jj; you bring the reviewed work into its target with jj.

workflow.value.folder.project.note: A value of the workflow option “Where cards are built” (glossary 2.6, G11).

workflow.value.folder.slots.text: Each card in its own folder
workflow.value.folder.slots.note: A value of the workflow option “Where cards are built” (glossary 2.6, G11). The folder is a slot, a worktree Combwork lends to the card or its lane (glossary 2.5: slot).

workflow.value.mergeInstall.always.note: A value of the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch”: before each card’s merge checks.

workflow.value.mergeInstall.alwaysCandid.note: The value “always” of the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch” in a project using jj (HI-2938): before the merge checks on each candidate (the commit Combwork builds for the user to integrate).

workflow.value.mergeInstall.onManifestCh.text: When the lock file or manifests change
workflow.value.mergeInstall.onManifestCh.note: A value of the workflow option “Install dependencies from scratch”: only when the project’s lock file or package manifests changed (glossary: lock file, as in the G15 value).

workflow.value.review.agent.note: A value of the workflow option for review (glossary 2.6, G1 and N1).

workflow.value.review.agentThenYou.note: A value of the workflow option for review (glossary 2.6, G1 and N1).

workflow.value.review.none.note: A value of the workflow option “Work is reviewed before it’s merged” (glossary 2.6, G1).

workflow.value.review.noneNone.note: A value of the workflow option “Who checks the work before it’s done”, for a project without version control (glossary 2.6, N1).

workflow.value.review.you.note: A value of the workflow option for review: you review (glossary 2.6, G1 and N1).

workflow.value.reviewerMode.lane.note: A value of the workflow option “Reviewers” (glossary 2.6, G17): each lane has its own reviewer agent.

workflow.value.reviewerMode.pool.note: A value of the workflow option “Reviewers” (glossary 2.6, G17): lanes share a pool of reviewer agents, each card going to the next free one.

workflow.value.sameness.change.note: A value of the workflow option “A pass survives a clean rebase” (glossary 2.6, G4).

workflow.value.sameness.exact.note: A value of the workflow option “A pass survives a clean rebase” (glossary 2.6, G4).

workflow.value.style.merge.note: A value of the workflow option “Merge style” (glossary 2.6, G6).

workflow.value.style.rebase.note: A value of the workflow option “Merge style” (glossary 2.6, G6; #1184): Combwork’s merge queue rebases the card’s commits onto the target branch and moves the branch forward to them, so the history stays linear, with no merge commit.

workflow.value.style.squash.note: A value of the workflow option “Merge style” (glossary 2.6, G6).
